approach.method_basis: The Parent runs two molecular graph searches. Each search keeps an evaluated center and its own episode labels, fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process, and generates descendants along bounded mutation and crossover paths. Their joint posterior draws compete in raw score units for the announced evaluation batch. Both predictors use a shared response amplitude estimated from all accepted labels in the current session. Purchased local progress expands or contracts each search; repeated failure at the smallest extent retires the episode. A restart currently picks the highest-scoring eligible unused root, or the least-recently-used root when every eligible root has been used, and starts a fresh model from that one accepted label.
approach.novelty: Add a structural feasibility test to that existing restart decision: within the inherited root-use tier, choose the highest-scoring accepted molecule whose count-fingerprint similarity is at most one half to both current centers. If none qualifies, use the original choice. This changes where a natural restart begins while preserving the singleton predictor and auction. The same-Parent conditioning sibling instead adds nearby accepted labels to a predictor at the original root; this experiment isolates relocation and measures whether its lower starting score earns useful global progress.

finding_summary.headline: Separated restart roots activated, but useful escape remains inconclusive after seed-1 interruption
finding_summary.insights:
This result rules out failure to move the reset roots or blanket denial of first feedback as explanations for the observed lack of useful progress. Structural displacement, new proposals and recovery from a weak local root can all occur without beating the session incumbent. The narrow literature borrowing—score ranking after a separation feasibility test—operated; the result does not evaluate the source method’s global surrogate or diverse-output objective. The surviving controller still starts each reset with one label and a constant predicted mean. A restart model that conditions on accepted evidence beyond that single label, or a search scheme that evaluates restart opportunity in terms of global improvement, is a different kind of intervention that could address that information gap; this experiment does not establish either as beneficial.

The molecular assessment also narrows the diagnosis: the generator already produces many ring systems and frameworks, so a universal shortage of scaffold diversity is unsupported. Yet 112 of 3,410 paid proposals were tiny fragments, 228 exceeded fifty heavy atoms, and unusual N-halogen connections remained frequent. Broad graph novelty often failed to preserve the useful connected group arrangements present in stronger molecules. Proposal operators that preserve those arrangements while changing scaffold or linker structure could address this distinct limitation; increasing geometric distance alone did not do so here. The missing seed-1 panel leaves the complete benefit test open, and this node does not overturn earlier findings or decide the future of the broader approach.
finding_summary.results:
The restart rule operated correctly in all 14 observed resets: 13 chose a different root and one kept the original choice. All satisfied the fixed separation condition, all received immediate feedback, and the inherited trigger and singleton model initialization were preserved. Mean distance from the nearer old center rose from 0.204 for the same-state original choices to 0.532, at a mean known starting-score cost of 0.176. The new episodes produced 6,140 identities absent from earlier fields and bought 627 evaluations, but only three evaluations improved the global best. Their total fresh global gain was 0.0012921, or 0.000002061 per paid evaluation, versus the Parent’s 0.000123063. Local recovery was much larger, totaling 0.64113, which does not establish useful escape.

Seeds 0 and 2 completed: their mean score was 0.571827 with population SD 0.021043, a paired difference of -0.005351 from the Parent and -0.046102 from the formal Anchor. Neither complete seed improved its macro score; among all 11 completed task endpoints, five fell and six tied the Parent. Seed 1 completed its first task, stopped during the second with exit143, and has no observations for the remaining three. These partial receipts remain evidence, but the full fifteen-endpoint macro and the registered joint benefit falsifier cannot be evaluated. The result therefore establishes activation and adverse observed benefit movement, while the overall registered intervention remains inconclusive.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families coexist with reactive N-halogen motifs, tiny fragments and oversized assemblies; seed 1 is incomplete.
molecular.overall_character:
This is a reading of n-7c404cb14467's observed Search molecules, not an activation or performance verdict. Seeds 0 and 2 each supply all five complete trajectories. Seed 1 supplies 300 zaleplon_mpo observations and only 230 deco_hop observations; its drd2_docking, median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo trajectory files are absent. Its execution receipt records exit code 143. The seed-1 partial evidence is retained, including its observed high-scoring molecules, without inventing an endpoint for the interrupted task or molecules for the absent tasks. The frozen comparison marks child_complete=false and paired_complete=false and has complete matched seeds 0 and 2. All fifteen published Parent n-7d1e6230ecce Search trajectories were available and read; incomplete Child coverage is not a missing Parent baseline. No Confirmation evidence is used.

The available trajectories contain 3530 recorded observations, including 3410 optimizer records. Structural counts below were calculated directly from those optimizer SMILES in memory with RDKit, excluding supplied initial records. All 3410 recorded optimizer molecules parse; this says nothing about rejected construction attempts or unbought candidate fields. Of these records, 112 have fewer than six heavy atoms and 228 have more than fifty. The task-level median sizes are substantially larger than fragment scale. Rings, aromatic heterocycles, amides, ketones, ethers, phenols and amines are plentiful, with both fused and bridged graphs. The digest's ring-closure rates span 0.9155 to 0.9862 and aromatic-presence rates span 0.9103 to 0.9810; these are per-molecule string indicators, not fractions of atoms. Every task's charged and stereocentre string rates are zero. Neutral SMILES nevertheless include potentially basic amines, so neither absence of formal charge nor absence of stereomarks establishes absence of ionizable groups or stereogenic centers.

Graph diversity is broad, although stronger molecules within a session often remain close to a recognizable family. Typed/generic scaffold counts below count unique nonempty RDKit Murcko scaffolds, with atom/bond typing removed for the generic version; their denominators are the observed ring-bearing optimizer records, not the full frozen panel. Diverse ring graphs do not establish broad synthetic accessibility. N-halogen, N-S and N-O connections, cumulenes, unusual small fused rings, and large repeated assemblies make synthetic plausibility questionable despite parseability. Several strong molecules have ordinary medicinal-chemistry features, but no synthesis, stability, binding mechanism or drug efficacy was measured here. Structural associations and Parent contrasts are not attribution to the restart component. All descriptions concern recorded evaluated proposals; within-field locality, unpurchased chemistry and post-reset exposure require the separate receipt analysis.

per_task.generated_character: All three task trajectories are present: 870 optimizer records have median 25.5 heavy atoms and range 1-55; 34/870 are below six and 1/870 above fifty. There are 824/870 ring-bearing and 806/870 aromatic molecules, with 357 typed and 202 generic scaffolds among the ring-bearing records. Higher-scoring molecules include substituted indole-like heteroaromatics carrying methoxy, methyl, nitrile and ketone/amide groups plus a second aryl or pyridyl ring. Seed 1's observed maximum is a 26-heavy-atom, three-ring methoxy/nitrile heteroaromatic ketone with an N-S substituent. Its close NH analogue has a more ordinary bond pattern. Seed 0 instead ends with a compact fused heteroaromatic/enamine family containing N-Cl; seed 2 explores indole carboxamides and later extensively cumulated unsaturation. These are chemically different outputs, not a ring-poor series. The Parent covers the same broad families; its complete task trajectories contain 298 typed and 161 generic scaffolds. More Child graph variants do not establish improved chemistry. The observed task maxima in seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.42570769607214154, 0.4867923180158012 and 0.41700086027236194, versus the Parent's 0.42762099872850584, 0.5423261445466404 and 0.4478476056206344. The seed-1 task comparison is observable even though its whole evaluation is incomplete.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 289/870 recorded optimizer molecules. The seed-0 and seed-2 high-scoring examples themselves include N-Cl attachments, so this concern cannot be dismissed as only low-score debris.

The digest reports a cumulated-double-bond rate of 0.1609; the trajectories contain 140 such records concentrated in seed 2. The late polyunsaturated chains and unusual heteroatom connections warrant stability and route questions, not automatic claims of impossibility.
Tiny fragments and an oversized tail coexist with the useful medium-sized families; no stereochemical configurations are encoded.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of the connected aryl/heteroaryl-carbonyl arrangement during edits is missing from many weaker outputs, although the stronger examples demonstrate that the generator can make it.

The observed library does not establish a routinely plausible alternative scaffold family that retains those stronger combinations without reactive N-halogen or cumulated-bond attachments; no unseen target-specific pharmacophore can be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-S molecule scores 0.4867923180158012, while the related NH compound scores 0.48660033404583897: this is not evidence that the unusual sulfur attachment is essential. A recorded truncated analogue retaining methoxy, nitrile and the N-S fused core but replacing the second heteroaryl-bearing ketone side with a short fluorinated side scores only 0.0026927905956525503. Tiny FS scores 0.0. These examples associate coherent, medium-sized heteroaromatic/carbonyl combinations with stronger scores, rather than simply more rings or more heteroatoms. The final seed-2 N-Cl/cumulene-rich proposal scores 0.2473162894768986, below that seed's observed best. This is a final proposal, not its final incumbent.

per_task.generated_character: The observed set has 800 optimizer records: complete seeds 0 and 2 plus only 220 optimizer records from seed 1. Heavy-atom median is 38, range 1-108; 21/800 fall below six and 203/800 exceed fifty. Rings and aromatic atoms are present in 777/800 records, containing 416 typed and 331 generic nonempty scaffolds. This is the strongest oversized-assembly tendency in the available panel. The seed-2 high-scoring family joins two fused N/O heteroaromatic carbonyl systems through NH and carries ketone, chloromethyl and imine/alkenyl side groups. Seed 1's observed high family is an NH-linked halogenated benzothiophene/aza-polycycle; seed 0 uses halogenated polyaza carbonyl heterocycles. Dense heteroaromatic cores are plausible medicinal-chemistry starting motifs, but repeated large assemblies, reactive appendages and unusual connections make the entire set less convincing. The Child's full seed-0 and seed-2 SMILES/score sequences equal the corresponding published Parent sequences; all 230 observed seed-1 rows equal the Parent prefix. The Parent's later seed-1 chemistry is additional exposure, not evidence of a completed Child comparison.
liabilities: The 203/800 molecules above fifty heavy atoms and the 108-heavy-atom maximum show that size expansion is a substantial output property, not a rare illustrative extreme.
Chloromethyl/haloalkyl groups, imines and densely linked heteroaromatic carbonyl systems raise reactivity and synthetic-route questions. Presence of these groups does not by itself prove instability.
There is no stereochemical specification and no synthetic accessibility measurement; interrupted seed-1 sampling prevents a full three-seed chemistry comparison.
missing_features: Many weak proposals lack the connected heteroaromatic architecture present in the stronger molecules; other proposals retain it only inside much larger concatenated structures. Consistent preservation at a manageable molecular size is not demonstrated across the set.

The observed equal-score side-chain variants do not identify a missing unique substituent or a required target scaffold. The evidence supports a need to explore coherent alternatives to repeated assemblies, not a prescription for an unseen objective-specific answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Simple fragments such as ClCl score 0.5, whereas the paired heteroaromatic carbonyl system reaches 0.6314459049544995. Multiple terminal side-chain variants, including chloromethyl/bromomethyl changes, share that value. A close recorded side-chain amide variant scores 0.6027917030768524. The seed-1 NH-linked sulfur/aza-ring family reaches 0.6251303441084463 before interruption. This associates substantial connected heteroaromatic architecture and its substitution pattern with stronger values, but does not show a monotonic reward for size, halogens or synthetic complexity. The final seed-2 proposal scores 0.61634565330557 while the incumbent remains higher.

per_task.generated_character: Only seeds 0 and 2 are observed: 580 optimizer records, median 28 heavy atoms, range 1-108, with 18/580 below six and 11/580 above fifty. There are 562/580 ring-bearing and 539/580 aromatic records, containing 255 typed and 168 generic nonempty scaffolds. Seed 0's 24-heavy-atom maximum joins a dialkylamino-substituted cyclohexene to a dichlorophenyl group. Halogenated aromatic surfaces and alkyl-rich amines can carry medicinal-chemistry liabilities, but no solubility, selectivity or safety measurement is available here.

The set does not consistently retain that arrangement while avoiding overbuilt bridged graphs or N-N-rich ring edits; stereochemical configurations of substituted saturated rings and benzylic centers are also not represented. The observed scores do not establish a reward for assigning those configurations.

Rings occur in 572/580 and aromatic atoms in 569/580, with 383 typed and 268 generic nonempty scaffolds. The stronger seed-0 family combines a fused nitrogen-containing aromatic system with a larger aza ring containing N-N and acyl functionality. Seed 2 combines a phenyl-substituted nitrogen heterocycle/diaza ring with an ethoxy-substituted aza ring fused to a four-membered dicarbonyl unit. The observed maxima contain 29 and 34 heavy atoms respectively. This is substantial heteroaromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry, not a lack of ring generation. The same maximum-scoring molecules and values occur in the corresponding Parent seeds: 0.21592303267069837 and 0.2266386345140889, despite some changed later proposals. Parent seed 1 is available, but the Child has no corresponding trajectory.
liabilities: The seed-2 high family includes a fused four-membered dicarbonyl unit; the seed-0 high family includes N-N/acyl connectivity in a larger ring. Both warrant specific synthetic-route and stability assessment rather than assuming that parseable aromatic notation makes them ordinary compounds.
Many nearby variants change several ring, bond and heteroatom features together, so the observed score differences cannot identify a single required group.
No stereochemical configuration is encoded; oversized concatenations and very small fragments remain present, although less dominant than the substantial ring systems.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of the stronger carbonyl/aza-ring/aryl connectivity through substantial ring edits is absent from many weaker variants, even though the generator explores numerous typed and generic scaffolds.

A broader set of routinely plausible alternative cores retaining the useful group arrangement is not established. Additional ring count, a particular unobserved scaffold or target-specific substituent cannot be justified from this score range.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The highest observed value is 0.2266386345140889. A related altered aza-ring/partially unsaturated carbocycle combination scores 0.18468000360467582, while methane scores 0.0 and methylamine 0.008773280079294957. The starting observed maximum is 0.1678386594791329. The limited upward gradient therefore follows particular connected aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangements; making any ring-rich molecule is insufficient. The final seed-2 modified aryl/aza-ring proposal scores 0.16914781383660782. The trajectories do not reveal an unseen structure that would complete the objective.

per_task.generated_character: Only seeds 0 and 2 are present: 580 optimizer records, median 28 heavy atoms, range 1-59, with 32/580 below six and 5/580 above fifty. There are 531/580 ring-bearing and 528/580 aromatic records, with 158 typed and 76 generic nonempty scaffolds. The stronger family is dominated by nitrogen-rich fused dicarbonyl heterocycles with fluorinated carbocyclic/heterocyclic substituents. Seed 0's 29-heavy-atom maximum combines an aminomethyl group with partially unsaturated rings, carbon-bound fluorine and several N-F bonds. Seed 2's 28-heavy-atom maximum has the same broad heteroaromatic dicarbonyl character with a fluorinated alkenyl chain and a hydroxy/fluoropyridyl substituent. Thus polar and amine functionality is available, but reactive N-fluorination is deeply embedded in the stronger family. The seed-0 maximum molecule and value, 0.7327195754462501, are identical to the Parent's. In seed 2, the Child's 0.48214377864515795 and the Parent's 0.5025353058534101 remain within related fluorinated heteroaromatic dicarbonyl chemistry. No Child seed-1 molecules are available.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 373/580 recorded optimizer molecules, including multiple N-F bonds in the strongest seed-0 molecule. These are unconventional reactive functionalities for an ordinary drug-like series.

Dicarbonyl heterocycles, unsaturated N-F rings, occasional N-S/N-O substitutions and very large fragment combinations give questionable synthetic plausibility despite complete parsing of the observed records.
The final low-scoring urea/aldehyde assemblies demonstrate loss of the stronger local arrangement; final proposal quality must not be confused with the retained incumbent.
missing_features: Preservation of the precise amino/polar-group arrangement during otherwise modest edits is missing from many low-scoring relatives; an aminomethyl group is demonstrably available and should not be described as universally absent.

The observed strong family does not demonstrate comparably strong alternatives using ordinary amine/carbon-bound fluorine connectivity in place of its repeated N-F motifs. This is a chemical coverage gap, not proof that replacing those bonds would raise the score.
Configured stereogenic saturated-ring products are absent from the encoded SMILES. The data do not demonstrate that stereochemical enumeration is rewarded.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminomethyl-bearing seed-0 molecule scores 0.7327195754462501. Its recorded ethyl-bearing counterpart, obtained structurally by replacing that terminal amino nitrogen with carbon, scores 5.621905359034732e-05. A recorded analogue with an added oxygen in the linkage to the unsaturated nitrogen ring scores 0.06387998583399676. These contrasts show sensitivity to the exact polar-group arrangement rather than a general benefit from adding fluorine or heteroatoms. An oversized 59-heavy-atom ester/thioester-derived assembly scores 2.3956869936426998e-105, and the final seed-2 urea/aldehyde-rich multiring proposal scores 9.136467403817658e-18. Strong values therefore coexist with a very broad low-score tail. The N-F bonds in the high molecule are observed tolerated features, not demonstrated causal requirements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-7c404cb14467, observed Search seeds 0 and 2 plus the available incomplete seed-1 records. Among 3410 recorded optimizer molecules, 112 have fewer than six heavy atoms and 228 have more than fifty. Tiny disconnected-from-the-useful-core fragments and oversized repeated assemblies appear alongside substantially smaller strong molecules. These are observed output counts, not counts of all attempted or unbought candidates, and the absent cells are not imputed.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a coherent molecular scale while changing chemical structure.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide structure-changing edits that preserve a connected scaffold and its useful group arrangement without requiring either drastic truncation or concatenation. Let current-session feedback determine useful molecular size; the observed tails do not justify a universal hard size cutoff or establish that size control will improve scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-7c404cb14467 under the same partial Search coverage. Direct bond inspection finds N-halogen connections in 790/3410 recorded optimizer molecules. Several high-scoring structures themselves contain N-Cl or multiple N-F bonds, while other strong analogues use ordinary NH and carbon-bound halogen groups. The digest also shows a substantial cumulated-bond subseries. High score and graph validity therefore do not establish synthetic plausibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically ordinary heteroatom and halogen diversification is not reliably separated from unusual N-halogen and heteroatom-heteroatom attachments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable alternatives that retain a useful ring system and polar-group placement while varying ordinary amine, amide, ether and carbon-bound halogen connectivity. Treat reactivity and route plausibility as chemistry diagnostics; do not assume that deleting an unusual bond improves the objective or infer a universal hard exclusion from this association.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-7c404cb14467, recorded Search trajectories with the same incomplete coverage. The observed higher subsets include linked heteroaromatic carbonyl systems, amine-bearing hydrophobic rings and precisely arranged amino/dicarbonyl motifs. Nearby recorded variants that truncate the second ring, replace a terminal amino group, insert a linker oxygen or rebuild an aza ring can score much lower. Typed and generic scaffold coverage is substantial, so a blanket lack of ring or scaffold generation is unsupported. These comparisons are observational and do not isolate a causal component.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph variation does not consistently preserve the functional-group arrangements associated with the generator's own stronger molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support scaffold and linker changes that can retain a session-supported donor/acceptor and attachment pattern while offering chemically different cores. Useful patterns must come from that session's accepted molecules and scores, without any task identity or fixed pharmacophore answer. Distinguish preservation of a promising chemical arrangement from mere graph novelty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-7c404cb14467, all five digest task subsets under partial Search coverage. Every stereocentre string rate is zero, while cited substituted saturated nitrogen rings and benzylic/halogenated centers can create stereochemical choices. Formal-charge string rates are also zero, but neutral amines are present; this is not evidence that ionizable chemistry is missing.
transferable_gaps.gap: The observed output does not encode the configurations of the stereogenic products it can generate.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly represent valid stereochemical choices when generating substituted saturated structures, using the permitted molecular representation and current-session feedback. This is an output-representation gap only: the trajectories provide no demonstration that assigning stereochemistry or changing ionization states is rewarded.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
